nodes.name: Co3O4@CoRuOx
aliases: cobalt-doped RuOx frameworks on Co3O4 nanocones

nodes.name: CC pretreatment and CoO hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The purchased CC was soaked in concentrated HNO3 at 25°C for 24 h to modify its surface with rich oxygen-containing functional groups and then washed with deionized water several times. Afterward, the cleaned CC (4.0×3.0 cm^-1) was immersed into a well-premixed aqueous solution (40 mL) containing Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.582 g), CO(NH2)2 (0.440 g) and NH4F (0.297 g). Immediately, the above solution was sealed into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and kept in an oven at 120°C for 8 h. After cooling to room temperature, the as-deposited CC was rinsed with water and ethanol for three times, and dried overnight in an oven at 60°C. Subsequently, the as-deposited CC was calcined under N2 atmosphere at 300°C for 2 h with a ramp rate of 10°C min^-1, resulting in CoO nanocones on CC (labeled as CoO).

nodes.procedure: Next, the obtained CoO was soaked into a 20 mL mixture of water and ethanol (Vwater/Vethanol = 1:1) containing 2-MIM (0.625 g), and kept in water bath at 30°C for 12 h, resulting in CoO wrapped with ZIF-67 on CC (labeled as CoO@ZIF-67).

nodes.name: Ru-cation exchange and air annealing
nodes.procedure: Thereafter, a piece of CoO@ZIF-67 was immersed into 5 mg mL^-1 RuCl₃ aqueous solution, maintained at 30°C for 30 min, and then taken out, rinsed with water and ethanol for three times, and dried overnight at 60°C. Finally, the product was calcined under air atmosphere at 300°C for 2 h with a ramp rate of 5°C min^-1, resulting in Co3O4 wrapped with cobalt-doped RuOx frameworks on CC (labeled as Co3O4@CoRuOx).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic peaks of Co₃O₄ (JCPDS 42-1467) and RuO₂ (JCPDS 40-1290); RuO₂ (110) and (101) peaks shift to higher angles by ≈0.28° and 0.36° due to Co doping induced lattice contraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic diffraction peaks assigned to Co₃O₄ (JCPDS Card No. 42-1467) and RuO₂ (JCPDS Card No. 40-1290) emerge in the XRD patterns... the diffraction peaks of RuO₂ (110) and (101) planes move slightly towards a higher angle, ≈0.28° and 0.36° respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals core-shell structure with polyhedrons on Co₃O₄ core and ≈15 nm nanoparticles on shell; interplanar spacings of RuO₂ (110) and (101) decrease from 0.318/0.256 nm to 0.309/0.241 nm confirming lattice contraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of Co₃O₄@CoRuOₓ show that a shell composed of many polyhedrons is tightly wrapped around Co₃O₄ core... the interplanar spacings of RuO₂ (110) and (101) planes decrease from 0.318 and 0.256 nm (pure RuO₂) to 0.309 and 0.241 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDX line-scanning confirms core-shell structure with Co/Ru ratio 1:1 in outer shell; elemental mapping shows uniform CoRuOₓ shell coverage on Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM-energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (STEM-EDX) line-scanning finely depicts the core-shell structure... The Co/Ru atom ratio at the outer shell is equal to 1:1... The distribution of Co, Ru, and O elements measured by the STEM-EDX mapping further verifies that CoRuOₓ shell uniformly covers the surface.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The content of Ru species is only 3.7 wt.% analyzed by the inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES, Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows characteristic Ru-O and Co-O peaks with synchronous redshift relative to commercial RuO₂ and Co₃O₄, indicating decreased electron density and higher oxidation states of Ru and Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic Ru-O and Co-O peaks emerge in the Raman spectra... The synchronous redshift of Ru-O and Co-O peaks is worthy of notice relative to the commercial RuO₂ and Co₃O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows Co 2p peaks shifted 0.75 eV higher (Co³⁺ 779.7 eV, Co²⁺ 781.2 eV), Ru 3p Ru(IV) peaks redshifted 0.8 eV, and O 1s with increased oxygen vacancies (531.2 eV) confirming Co doping effect.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Co 2p spectrum of Co₃O₄@CoRuOₓ is deconvoluted into six sub-peaks, corresponding to the spin orbitals of Co 2p₃/₂ (Co³⁺ at 779.7 eV, Co²⁺ at 781.2 eV)... shift of ≈0.75 eV to the high binding energy occurs... Only the peaks assigned to Ru (IV) species present a distinct redshift of 0.8 eV... In O 1s XPS of Co₃O₄@CoRuOₓ... Oᵥ (& O-H) (531.2 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows clear resonance signals confirming oxygen vacancies from Co doping in RuO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectrum of Co₃O₄@CoRuOₓ correspondingly shows clear resonance signals compared with EPR inactive RuO₂ and EPR low activity Co₃O₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: Valence band XPS shows VB maximum at ≈0.05 eV from Fermi level (closest among catalysts), indicating higher electron density near Fermi level for enhanced OER electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The maximum VB value of Co₃O₄@CoRuOₓ is ≈0.05 eV, the closest to the Fermi level (E_f, set to 0 eV) among all catalysts, illustrating a higher electron density around the Fermi level.
